title: fix(cli): `--database-driver` stops refusing `mysql` and `sqlite-wasm` at parse time (#6860)
body:
Fixes #6860.

## This is a live user-visible defect, not docs lag

#6345 recorded this as a "help text is missing two entries" item. That framing is
**wrong**, and I disproved it by measurement before changing anything.

`--database-driver` is declared with oclif's `options:`, which is an **enforced
allowlist**, not a help string. A value outside it is rejected during flag
parsing — the command body never runs. Measured on unmodified `origin/main`
(659526212), with the real built binary:

```
$ os start --database-driver mysql
 ›   Error: Expected --database-driver=mysql to be one of: sqlite, turso,
 ›   postgres, mongodb, memory
 ›   See more help with --help                                          # exit 2
```

All four combinations refuse identically — `start`/`dev` × `mysql`/`sqlite-wasm`,
exit 2 every time.

The same drivers work through the env var, on the same command:

```
$ OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=mysql os start
🗄️ Database: mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/osdb
  ✗ datasource 'default': connect failed — connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3306
                                        # reached the body; only the connect failed

$ OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite-wasm os start
  ✓ Server is ready                     # boots and serves
```

One thing, two answers — and the flag's answer arrives in oclif's generic
vocabulary rather than anything this repo wrote, so it reads as "ObjectStack has
no MySQL driver" instead of "this flag's list is stale". The operator's actual
next move (drop the flag, export the env var) is not one the message suggests.

## The fix

Add `mysql` and `sqlite-wasm` to **both** `options:` allowlists — the flag is
declared once in `start.ts` and once in `dev.ts` — and align the two
`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` flag tables to the set actually accepted. The
`OS_DATABASE_DRIVER` row in `environment-variables.mdx` already listed the full
set and is untouched.

After the fix, same binary, all four combinations:

| command | driver | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `os start` | `mysql` | exit 2 at parse | resolves mysql, fails only on the real connect |
| `os start` | `sqlite-wasm` | exit 2 at parse | `✓ Server is ready` |
| `os dev` | `mysql` | exit 2 at parse | resolves mysql, fails only on the real connect |
| `os dev` | `sqlite-wasm` | exit 2 at parse | `✓ Server is ready` |

## The pin

`packages/cli/src/commands/database-driver-allowlist.pin.test.ts` asserts the
**agreement** between the allowlist and the driver kinds `resolveStorageDefinition`
produces. It deliberately does not restate a list: a hard-coded expectation would
just relocate the divergence into the test, so a future driver would go missing
from the flag *and* from the test at once, silently. Both sides are derived from
the code that owns them:

- the allowlist, read off the oclif flag definitions;
- the driver kinds, by scanning `storage-driver.ts` for candidate tokens with a
  deliberately over-broad net and then using `resolveStorageDefinition` **itself**
  as the oracle for which are real — 24 candidates scanned → 17 recognized tokens
  → 7 canonical `driverId`s. Junk (`safe`, `factory`, `better-sqlite3`, …) washes
  out on its own, so the derivation survives the dispatch being rewritten.

Both commands are covered, because the duplicated declaration is exactly how they
can drift from each other as well as from the resolver. `isDev: false` is
load-bearing — in dev mode an unrecognized kind falls through to the sqlite
default, which would make every token look recognized and the whole derivation
vacuous.

## Reverse verification

Predicted **before** running: revert only the two `options:` arrays, keep the test
⇒ **4 red of 10**, two per command (the agreement assertion; the parse assertion,
which iterates the derived set so `mysql`/`sqlite-wasm` throw).

Measured: **4 failed | 6 passed**, exactly those four, with the predicted
directions — the set diff reported `mysql` and `sqlite-wasm` missing, and the parse
failures carried `Expected --database-driver=sqlite-wasm to be one of: sqlite,
turso, postgres, mongodb, memory`. Restored ⇒ 10/10.

Honestly excluded — **green in both directions, not evidence for this fix**:

- `derives a non-empty set …` (×1) — a guard on the derivation itself.
- `lists only canonical kinds …` (×2) — catches the opposite bug (an alias or a
  phantom driver in the allowlist), which #6860 is not.
- `still refuses a value that is not a driver kind` (×2) — `options:` stayed
  enforced; only its contents shrank.
- `start and dev offer the same kinds as each other` (×1) — both commands were
  wrong the *same* way, so this parity check was green while the defect was live.

Also stated plainly: **the docs half has no pin.** Reverting the two table rows
goes green everywhere. No repo gate compares doc tables to `options:`, and building
one is outside this card's scope.

## Gates

Run on the **merged** result (`origin/main` @ 25ab57bd5 merged in, clean, no
conflicts; full `turbo run build` closure green first, as `lint.yml` does):

- `pnpm lint` — pass
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` — pass
- all **43** `check:*` targets from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` — pass, including
  `check:type-check-debt` and `check:i18n-coverage` (both need the build closure)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test` — **1042 passed, 2 failed**

The 2 failures are in `src/utils/schema-migrate.pending-render.test.ts`, a file
this PR does not touch. They are `Test timed out in 5000ms` and a cascade of it
(the timed-out render's output bleeds into the next test's shared capture buffer).
**Confirmed pre-existing**, not load-excused: the same 2 tests fail the same way on
a pristine `origin/main` compare worktree with its own full build — 2 failed | 7
passed on both sides, identical. The box is shared with other agents today; one
earlier `check:query-options-erasure` red was likewise load-induced and passes
clean.

## Scope

Deliberately narrow, per the maintainer's ruling. No vocabulary convergence, no
`packages/spec`, no `standalone-stack.ts`. The resolver still accepts aliases
(`pg`, `mysql2`, `libsql`, `mingo`, `wasm`, …) the flag does not offer, and the pin
is written so that stays true — an alias collapses to its canonical id and is not
demanded of the flag. Deriving the allowlist from a shared alias table remains
#6345's work and will refactor these lines away; that rework is known and accepted.

Changeset: **patch** on `@objectstack/cli`. No driver is added — `mysql` and
`sqlite-wasm` already worked and were already reachable via `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER`;
what was broken was parity between two entry points to the same capability. The
change is strictly widening, so every invocation that parsed before still parses
identically and there is nothing to migrate.

Files: `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts`,
`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, the new pin test, the changeset.
